claim.pdf_says: NOTE 1, NOTE 2 and NOTE 3 are printed indented to the body indent of General rule 6) ('If an attempt is made to change the address of a data item containing a data-item subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause, the EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT exception condition is set to exist...'), i.e. they are sub-content of that rule.
claim.markdown_says:
6) If an attempt is made to change the address of a data item containing a data-item subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause, the EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT exception condition is set to exist. The ability to detect this is processor dependent.

NOTE 2 In the event that it is not possible to detect this situation, ...

NOTE 3 Rather than pass data items subject to APPLY COMMIT statements in linkage, ...
claim.why_it_matters: The three NOTEs are emitted flush left instead of indented under rule 6), detaching them from their parent rule. The transcription's own convention elsewhere keeps rule-scoped notes indented (page 346 'NOTE  As described in 13.4.5 ...' and page 354 'NOTE 1 / NOTE 2' under 12.4.5.8.4 General rule 1, both indented three spaces), so a reader scanning 12.4.6.3.4 cannot tell whether these notes qualify rule 6) or the whole General rules clause.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. The claim's two factual observations are each correct in isolation, but the difference is pure leading whitespace and the stated rationale is measurably wrong.

1) NO TEXT IS LOST, MOVED, OR REATTACHED. I rendered page 364 at 300 dpi and read it against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. Every word of General rule 6) and of NOTE 1, NOTE 2 and NOTE 3 is present in the markdown, verbatim, in the printed order, in the same subclause (12.4.6.3.4 General rules), immediately following rule 6). Nothing is attached to a different rule, a different clause, or a different page. The sole delta is that the markdown NOTE lines begin at column 0 while the PDF sets them at rule 6)'s body indent. That is formatting, which the rejection criteria exclude ('the difference is only page-break furniture, line wrapping, hyphenation, or formatting').

2) THE PDF OBSERVATION IS CONFIRMED BUT IMMATERIAL. In the render, the numeral '6)' sits at the rule-number margin and its body text starts one indent stop right; NOTE 1/2/3 start at that same body-text stop. So yes, the printed page indents them under rule 6). No glyph, choice indicator, or word is affected.

3) THE CLAIM'S SUPPORTING PREMISE IS FALSE. The claim asserts 'the transcription's own convention elsewhere keeps rule-scoped notes indented' and cites pages 346 and 354. Those two pages do indent, but they are the minority. Scanning all 395 NOTE lines in specs/ISO_COBOL.md and isolating those in a numbered-rule context (previous non-blank line is a numbered rule or another NOTE): 111 are flush left versus 51 indented — flush left prevails better than 2:1. Only 91 of 395 NOTE lines in the whole file carry any indentation. Page 364 therefore follows the transcription's dominant treatment; pages 346 and 354 are the cherry-picked exceptions. There is no convention here to violate, so the claimed 'detaching' has no baseline to detach from.

4) THE ALLEGED READER AMBIGUITY DOES NOT EXIST IN CONTEXT. Rule 6) is the LAST General rule of 12.4.6.3.4 — the markdown continues (after the page-364 separator) with '## 12.4.6.4 SAME clause' on page 365, and there is no rule 7). So the reader cannot mis-scope the NOTEs onto a following rule, and 'rule 6) versus the whole General rules clause' is a distinction without a difference when rule 6) is the clause's final rule. The NOTE text is self-scoping anyway: NOTE 1 'This will prevent the situation where a data item subject to the APPLY COMMIT clause is passed to a called program ... attempts to change the address of that data item' and NOTE 3 'would protect them from inadvertent addressing changes' plainly discuss rule 6)'s address-change scenario and nothing else.

5) NO NORMATIVE CONTENT IS AT RISK. NOTEs in ISO/IEC drafting are informative, not normative. Even a genuinely mis-scoped NOTE would alter no conformance requirement, no syntax rule, and no general rule. Nothing a compiler implements changes. The claim's own severity ('cosmetic') concedes the point.

Verdict: presentation-only whitespace difference with a false convention premise and a non-existent ambiguity. Not a content discrepancy. If the project ever wants uniform NOTE indentation it is a global style normalization across ~111 sites, not a page-364 transcription defect.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The PDF does indent NOTE 1/2/3 to General rule 6)'s body indent and the markdown does render them flush left, but all three NOTEs plus rule 6) are transcribed verbatim, in order, in the correct subclause, with no text lost or reattached. The difference is leading whitespace only. The claim's premise that the transcription conventionally indents rule-scoped NOTEs is false: across specs/ISO_COBOL.md, rule-adjacent NOTE lines are flush left 111 times versus indented 51 times, so page 364 matches the prevailing treatment and pages 346/354 are the exceptions. The claimed ambiguity is also absent — rule 6) is the final General rule of 12.4.6.3.4 (12.4.6.4 SAME clause follows), so there is no subsequent rule the NOTEs could be misread against, and NOTEs are informative and carry no normative weight in any case.
